extracted.intended_audience: environmental advocates, affected communities, state and local agencies receiving federal funding, journalists, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: A press-release style summary of the EPA's updated Title VI guidance describing procedural safeguards recipients of federal funds should implement to prevent discrimination and support environmental justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure adequate public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: State and local government entities receiving federal funding must ensure adequate public participation in their programs and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance focuses on ensuring robust and accessible public participation as a procedural safeguard; Earthjustice and quoted advocates emphasize that strong public participation helps 'daylight persistent and systemic harms' and enables communities to better advocate for their health and well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access for Limited English Proficiency (LEP) community members
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide access for Limited English Proficiency community members so they can meaningfully participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA guidance highlights LEP access as a key area; ensuring language access is presented as essential to equitable participation and complaint processes for affected communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of population and community data (federal data collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should collect population and community-level data to support transparency and identify disproportionate impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page quotes advocates calling the EPA's acknowledgement of the 'dire need for federal data collection' an important step toward transparency. NAACP remarks stress that data collection and transparency are necessary so agencies and federal funds recipients can ensure equity for frontline communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring of a non-discrimination coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies and funding recipients should hire a non-discrimination coordinator to oversee compliance with Title VI procedural requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance specifically calls out hiring a non-discrimination coordinator as a safeguard; Earthjustice frames this as one of the operational practices that will help recipients comply with Title VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination by federal grant recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Title VI prohibits recipients of federal grants from discriminating based on race, color, or national origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explains that residents can petition federal agencies (such as the EPA) to investigate and act against state and local agencies that discriminate or allow practices creating disproportionate harm; these procedural protections are described as essential to addressing systemic environmental injustices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural safeguards enabling petitions and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural safeguards should allow residents to petition federal agencies to investigate and remedy discriminatory practices by recipients of federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earthjustice frames these safeguards as essential for ensuring equitable treatment and enabling communities to prompt federal investigation and action when state or local agencies discriminate or permit disproportionate harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and use Title VI as an environmental-justice tool (including disparate-impact considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance affirms Title VI's role in addressing environmental justice, including issues related to disparate impact, even as legal challenges to disparate-impact enforcement continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes ongoing litigation and a preliminary injunction that prohibits the EPA and DOJ from enforcing disparate impact-based requirements against Louisiana; it presents the guidance as a 'useful step' while acknowledging the need for stronger federal defense and enforcement of Title VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement best practices and stopgaps to mitigate environmental harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should adopt best practices and stopgaps (procedural measures) to mitigate environmental harms that disproportionately affect protected communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotations from advocacy groups describe the guidance as helping agencies implement 'best practices' and 'stopgaps to mitigate environmental harms,' stressing that while procedural safeguards won't eradicate environmental racism, they are practical steps to improve accountability and community protections.
